subtopics.name: Strategies to Increase Food Production & Crop Yield

parts.problem_md:
Figure 3.2 shows plants surrounded by a layer of mulch.

![Photograph showing rows of young green crops growing through a thick layer of dry straw and plant stems covering the soil across a large field, illustrating organic mulch around the plants.](assets/001-photograph-showing-rows-of-young-green-crops-gro.jpg)

*Figure 3.2 Volker Prasuhn, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons*

Describe four ways that mulch increases crop yield.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Any **four** from:
> 
> - It reduces the growth of weeds, so there is less competition with the crop
> - It reduces evaporation, so the soil keeps more moisture
> - It reduces surface run-off
> - It reduces soil erosion
> - It adds organic nutrients to the soil as it breaks down
> - It improves the soil, for example its drainage
> - It reduces damage from pests
> - It protects roots from extreme heat or cold
> 
> **[4 marks]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> - Each way must be a different idea. Link each one to the crop, for example 'reduces evaporation, so the soil keeps more water for the crops'.

parts.problem_md:
The scientist investigates the effect of three different fertilisers on the crop yield of maize plants.

Table 3.1 shows the results of the investigation.

| fertiliser used | formula for ion | days until harvest | crop yield / thousand kg per Ha |
|---|---|---|---|
| nitrate | .......... | 94 | 31 |
| phosphate | .......... | 98 | 28 |
| potassium | K⁺ | 95 | 25 |
| control |   | 96 | 18 |

Complete Table 3.1.
parts.solution_md:
Nitrate: **NO₃⁻**  **[1 mark]**

Phosphate: **PO₄³⁻**  **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> - Give the ion, including its charge. 'Nitrogen' and 'phosphorus' are elements, not the ions in the fertiliser, so they do not score.
